endowment_summary: Showed good natural karting ability from age 10 and won the Volant Elf scholarship, but was not a prodigy; initially preferred football and was an indifferent kart racer in early attempts. Trained as a mechanic and worked at a garage while karting, showing practical aptitude rather than exceptional cognitive or creative talent.
inherited_summary: Father Philippe was a mechanic who ran a garage and did hillclimbs in a Ferrari; both parents were hillclimbers. Working-class family in Lyon with direct motorsport immersion through the father's garage and racing background.
ecosystem_summary: Won the prestigious Volant Elf scholarship at Paul Ricard in 1987, funding entry into Formula Renault. French motorsport pipeline with Winfield Racing School, Tony Kart contact at 13, and progression through French F3 and F3000 to F1.

endowment_summary: Candidate master of sports in gymnastics by sixth grade, providing physical advantages for aerobatics. Started flying at 19 relatively late, but progressed rapidly to national champion by 1991. Above-average physical aptitude and determination, though not a traditional prodigy.
inherited_summary: Daughter of ordinary workers in Shchuchinsk, Kazakhstan — father was a taxi driver/gamekeeper, mother a factory worker and gas station operator. No aviation background; working-class origin with no domain connections.
ecosystem_summary: Soviet DOSAAF aviation club system provided free access to aircraft and training. Coach Leonid Solodovnikov provided sustained individualized training. The state sports infrastructure gave her access to elite-level competition and the Russian national aerobatic team.

endowment_summary: Started skiing at age 3 with homemade skis, coached by his father. Won the prestigious Topolino race at 14 and joined the Italian national team at 17. Exceptional early skiing talent recognized as one of the greatest in decades.
inherited_summary: Family owned the Hotel Bella Vista in Trafoi, directly on the ski slopes. Father Georg was a ski instructor who operated a ski lift on the Stelvio Pass and coached him from age 3. Significant domain immersion through family business and father's profession.
ecosystem_summary: Grew up at Trafoi on the Stelvio Pass glacier, enabling year-round skiing and observation of national teams training. Italian national team at 17, Fiamme Gialle club. Perfect geography for alpine skiing development in South Tyrol.

endowment_summary: Started playing at age 5 with his brother in a basement; called the 'Mozart of table tennis.' Made allsvenskan debut at 12, won Swedish senior championship at 15 (youngest ever), reached European Championship final at 16. Exceptional natural ball feel and prodigy-level early achievement.
inherited_summary: Parents were actively involved at Spårvägens BTK club — father served as club chairman, mother sold coffee at events. Stable working/middle-class Stockholm family with deep club involvement, though not wealthy or domain professionals.
ecosystem_summary: Spårvägens BTK elite club culture in Stockholm, intense sibling competition with older brother Kjell-Åke from age 5. Pivotal training camp in China at age 14 — once-in-a-generation exposure to elite Chinese table tennis methodology. Stockholm's strong table tennis culture.

endowment_summary: Austrian Junior Champion at 16, won Arlberg-Kandahar race the same year, and World Championship downhill gold at 18. Exceptional early skiing talent confirmed by rapid rise to world champion as a teenager.
inherited_summary: Grew up in Kitzbühel near the Hahnenkamm course, one of the world's premier alpine skiing venues. No specific family wealth or skiing background documented, but the geographic immersion provided significant advantage.
ecosystem_summary: Kitzbüheler Ski Club and the Kitzbühel skiing culture provided daily access to world-class courses. Austrian ski team system with its deep development pipeline. Growing up in one of the world's premier alpine skiing towns was a frontier geography advantage.

endowment_summary: Showed natural driving ability from early teens, winning the Suzuka Circuit series as a rookie in 1973. Good aptitude for racing but started relatively late at 16 and developed through persistence rather than prodigy-level talent.
inherited_summary: Born to a farming family outside Okazaki with no racing background whatsoever. Had to secretly drive cars in the family garden, hiding from his father. Active disadvantage of no domain connections or resources.
ecosystem_summary: Suzuka Circuit, located near his home in Aichi prefecture, provided access to competitive racing. The Honda partnership through Japanese Formula Two gave him five championships with Honda V6 engines. Japanese racing pipeline was the key ecosystem advantage.

endowment_summary: Started skiing at age 3, made World Cup debut at 15, and earned first World Cup podium at 18. Exceptional early talent reaching elite international competition as a teenager, though she described herself as never reaching childhood friend Janica Kostelić's level early on.
inherited_summary: Family described as 'very average Slovenian' with limited resources, often choosing between expenses. No particular wealth or skiing family background. Modest circumstances in a small village.
ecosystem_summary: Crna na Koroškem village where skiing was the dominant sport, Crna Ski Club, and the Slovenian national team pipeline. World Cup exposure at 15 provided early elite competition access. Local skiing culture and national team support were key ecosystem advantages.

endowment_summary: Took up golf at 5, won first state event at 6, first national at 7, and captured five consecutive Junior World Golf Championship titles. NCAA Player of the Year as a freshman at Arizona. Prodigy-level dominance from a very young age with record-setting junior career.
inherited_summary: Father was a real estate developer, mother an artist. Grew up in a small house overlooking Guadalajara Country Club — a playground paradise. Upper-middle class Mexican family with access to golf facilities and supportive parents who took her to the course.
ecosystem_summary: University of Arizona golf scholarship with NCAA pipeline, local PGA golfer Rafael Alarcon as mentor from age 8. Guadalajara Country Club access. Strong collegiate golf system that developed her talent before turning professional.

endowment_summary: Started playing at 4, described as 'spectacular' at 4-5 years old. Youngest ATP winner since 2008 at 18, won US Open at 19 becoming youngest world No. 1 in ATP history. Prodigy-level talent recognized by IMG at 11 and Ferrero as 'something different.'
inherited_summary: Father was a tennis coach and club administrator at Real Sociedad Club de Campo de Murcia; great-uncle built the club. Tennis family where father played but couldn't afford to pursue professionally. Middle-class family with direct domain immersion.
ecosystem_summary: Juan Carlos Ferrero — former world No. 1 and French Open champion — as full-time mentor from age 15 at his academy in Villena. IMG signing at 11-12. Spanish tennis ecosystem. Perfect timing entering the ATP at a transitional moment. Once-in-a-generation mentor arrangement.

endowment_summary: Recognized as a musical genius almost from birth — could recognize musical notes on paper at 6 months, playing complete songs at 3. Classical piano prodigy funded by local benefactors. Attended Juilliard. Exceptional, trajectory-changing musical endowment despite severe environmental constraints.
inherited_summary: Born to a barber/handyman father and minister mother in Tryon, North Carolina, in the Jim Crow-segregated South. Sixth of eight children in a poor African-American family. Active disadvantage of poverty and racial discrimination.
ecosystem_summary: Local white benefactors established the Eunice Waymon Fund to finance her education. Allen High School for Girls in Asheville, Juilliard summer program. However, Curtis Institute rejection (attributed to racism) was a devastating ecosystem disadvantage. Private lessons with Curtis professor Sokoloff partially compensated.

endowment_summary: Made first-team debut at 16, played for England Schoolboys at Wembley before 90,000. Leicester chose to sell World Cup winner Gordon Banks to keep the teenage Shilton. Exceptional early goalkeeping talent recognized and promoted rapidly.
inherited_summary: Working-class Leicester family with no particular advantages. Boyhood fan who grew up watching matches at Filbert Street. No domain connections or wealth, but stable supportive family environment.
ecosystem_summary: Leicester City youth system from age 13, idolized and was mentored by Gordon Banks — England's World Cup-winning goalkeeper. Filbert Street immersion and English football pipeline. The club's willingness to promote a 16-year-old over a World Cup winner was extraordinary.

endowment_summary: Started skating at 7, experimented with dancing on ice independently. Won Canadian Junior Championship at 15. Developed a revolutionary artistic style that transformed men's figure skating. Exceptional creative and athletic talent, though not a traditional technical prodigy.
inherited_summary: Middle-class parents — father WWII veteran, mother painter who was domineering. Family supported his ambitions, driving thousands of miles for competitions. No skating background but supportive enough to enable training.
ecosystem_summary: Eva Vasak recognized his talent at 11 and coached him for free for eight years. Ellen Burka — legendary coach and mother of world champion Petra Burka — later trained him, with Cranston living in her basement for seven years. Canadian skating system provided competitive structure.

endowment_summary: Discovered acting at 20 after seeing a Molière production, having previously been more interested in cars and playing cards. No early prodigy evidence; talent emerged through training at IDHEC and drama classes. Above-average ability but not exceptional early endowment.
inherited_summary: Son of a wealthy food industrialist father (Raoul Trintignant) who was also a Resistance fighter and mayor. Mother from a rich family in Bollène. Illustrious family — uncles Maurice and Louis were celebrated racing drivers. Significant wealth and family name recognition.
ecosystem_summary: IDHEC film school in Paris, drama classes with Charles Dullin and Tania Balachova. Paris cinema ecosystem at the dawn of the French New Wave. Well-connected family enabled move to Paris and access to elite training institutions.

endowment_summary: Recognized as a 'great talent' in modern pentathlon, competing at the 1968 Olympics at 21 and winning World Championship silver at 20. Good natural athletic ability across multiple sports, but no prodigy-level evidence documented.
inherited_summary: No family background details are documented. Born in Enskede, Stockholm. No evidence of particular family advantages or disadvantages in the available record.
ecosystem_summary: K1 IF and Djurgårdens IF — elite Stockholm sports clubs. Swedish modern pentathlon system was one of the world's strongest. Multi-sport athletic environment in Stockholm with access to fencing, shooting, riding, swimming, and running facilities.

endowment_summary: Showed exceptional musical talent from childhood — writing music in his ABC book at 6, with perfect pitch confirmed by his great aunt Krushelnytska. Entered Lviv Music School at 7. Significant natural musical endowment recognized by world-class musicians early.
inherited_summary: Born into a family of Ukrainian intellectuals in Lviv. Parents were both University of Vienna-educated (father historian/ethnographer, mother chemist). Great aunt was Solomiya Krushelnytska, one of the world's brightest soprano opera stars. Significant intellectual and musical lineage.
ecosystem_summary: Lviv Conservatory and Moscow Conservatory postgraduate program under Dmitry Kabalevsky — elite institutional training. However, deportation to Siberia at age 9 (1947) interrupted education for 8 years, an active disadvantage. Teachers continued giving lessons in exile, partially mitigating the disruption.

endowment_summary: Gold medalist from gymnasium, organized school events, and showed communication talent from youth by 'commentating' on neighborhood football matches. Above-average ability but no exceptional or prodigy-level evidence.
inherited_summary: Father was a colonel, mother a school nutrition inspector for 26 years. Stable middle-class family in Kyiv's Troyeshchyna district. Modest but supportive family environment with no media industry connections.
ecosystem_summary: KVN student team at National Aviation University provided performing experience. National TV platform (UA:PBC) discovered him through a university concert producer. Kyiv as a media center and early Eurovision involvement provided career acceleration, though no elite mentors or institutions.

endowment_summary: Began helping in the workshop at age 8 and chose to continue the family craft. Showed talent in design coffin making and artistic innovation, but no prodigy-level evidence. Above-average craft ability and dedication to the family tradition.
inherited_summary: Grandson of Seth Kane Kwei, the inventor of Ghanaian fantasy coffins — an internationally recognized art form. Family workshop with global reputation provided direct domain immersion and a ready-made internationally known brand to inherit.
ecosystem_summary: Family workshop in Teshie with established tradition and international recognition. Teshie craft community with multiple workshops. However, limited formal artistic education or access to elite art institutions. The workshop itself was the primary ecosystem.

endowment_summary: Recognized as a future talent at 13 when joining Újpesti Dózsa ('this kid will be someone'). Developed over a decade before senior national team debut at 23. Good natural ability with tall, left-handed build advantageous for sabre, but not a prodigy.
inherited_summary: No family background details are documented in available sources. Born in Budapest with no evidence of particular family advantages or domain connections.
ecosystem_summary: Újpesti TE (Újpesti Dózsa) — one of Hungary's top fencing clubs. Coach Csaba Zarándi mentored him from 13 through his Olympic gold. Hungary's deep sabre fencing tradition and national team pipeline provided elite competitive environment.

endowment_summary: Spotted for good kinaesthesia at age 7, distinguished herself in domestic competitions as a teenager. Won Asian Games bronze at 17 and Olympic gold at 19. Exceptional gymnastic talent, particularly in vault, recognized early by the state system.
inherited_summary: Father absent, mother worked as a cook at the Pyongyang Sports Club. Modest background in Hamhung, an industrial city in North Korea. Active disadvantage of poverty and state-controlled environment with limited personal freedom.
ecosystem_summary: North Korean state sports system identified her at 7 and channeled her into a juvenile sports school. Pyongyang Sports Club provided elite training. Twin sister Hong Su-jong was also an elite gymnast, providing a high-trust peer environment. State-funded full-time training pipeline.

endowment_summary: Good footballer who debuted for Japan at the 1964 Olympics and was selected JSL Best Eleven in 1966 and 1967. Solid professional ability but no exceptional early talent or prodigy evidence documented.
inherited_summary: Born in Hiroshima Prefecture; no family background details are documented. No evidence of particular family advantages or domain connections in the available record.
ecosystem_summary: Yawata Steel (later Nippon Steel) — one of Japan's top corporate football clubs in the 1960s. The 1964 Tokyo Olympics provided national team exposure. Japan Soccer League pipeline gave him a structured professional environment at a key moment in Japanese football development.

endowment_summary: Won 255 of 267 bouts in his career. Became the first Soviet boxer to win a European title at 21 and Olympic gold at 24. Exceptional boxing ability with an outstanding competitive record, though started at 14 rather than as a young child.
inherited_summary: Fourth child of a teacher (mother) and laborer (father) in Yerevan, Armenia. Modest family with no boxing background. Active disadvantage of limited resources and large family.
ecosystem_summary: Coaches Artyom Arutyunov and Edward Aristakesyan provided quality training. Trudovye Rezervy (Labor Reserves) sports club and Soviet national team pipeline gave structured development. Soviet boxing system provided elite competition access and state support.

endowment_summary: Made short films from age 13 using 8mm film and stop-motion animation. Won a CalArts scholarship based on his student film 'Stalk of the Celery Monster.' Exceptional creative vision and artistic output from a young age, though not a traditional academic prodigy.
inherited_summary: Father was a former minor league baseball player who worked for Burbank Parks and Recreation; mother owned a cat-themed gift shop. Suburban Burbank family with no entertainment industry connections. Described his childhood as a 'private hell' — not close with parents.
ecosystem_summary: CalArts — Walt Disney's premier animation program — on scholarship. Disney apprenticeship directly from student work. Growing up in Burbank near major studios. Disney funded his short film 'Vincent' (1982) narrated by Vincent Price. Once-in-a-generation institutional pipeline from CalArts to Disney.

endowment_summary: Won his first bike race and then 18 of 36 races in his third year. Showed immediate natural cycling talent from age 15. Nicknamed 'Le Professeur' for his intelligence. Won Tour de France at 22 on first attempt — exceptional natural ability.
inherited_summary: Working-class family in Paris; father was a foreman in a metalworks factory. Parents actively opposed his cycling career, forcing him to race secretly. Active disadvantage of parental opposition and no cycling family background.
ecosystem_summary: Spotted by Cyrille Guimard, one of cycling's top directors, who placed him on the Renault-Elf team alongside Bernard Hinault. Joinville battalion (French army's elite sporting unit) provided training time. French cycling culture and the Guimard mentorship were trajectory-changing.

endowment_summary: Considered an opera prodigy by age 9, received classical voice, guitar, and piano training. Sang in theater choir and with the Lacomy singers. Exceptional vocal talent recognized early, though she failed the East German Actors School admission at 17.
inherited_summary: Mother Eva-Maria Hagen was a famous film actress called the 'Brigitte Bardot of the GDR.' Father Hans Oliva-Hagen was a screenwriter. Stepfather Wolf Biermann was a prominent dissident singer-songwriter. East German cultural elite family with direct CBS Records connection through stepfather.
ecosystem_summary: East German cultural elite provided early performing opportunities in films alongside her mother. Stepfather Wolf Biermann's CBS Records connection directly led to her record deal. Emigration to West Germany enabled exploration of London punk scene and formation of Nina Hagen Band in Hamburg.

endowment_summary: No evidence of exceptional cognitive, creative, or domain-specific ability. Physical appearance and willingness to work in adult entertainment were her primary assets. No prodigy or above-average talent indicators in any traditional sense.
inherited_summary: Born in 's-Gravendeel, Netherlands to a working-class family. Father in advertising, mother homemaker. Dropped out of school early, moved in with boyfriend at 17, worked as barmaid and prostitute at 19. Active economic disadvantage.
ecosystem_summary: Dutch model agency found her work in Italy. Rocco Siffredi connected her to adult film industry. Growth of the adult entertainment industry in the early 1990s provided opportunity. No elite institutions or mentors in a traditional sense.

endowment_summary: Showed good sprinting ability and power, developed through the Soviet sports system. Won the points classification at the 1988 Peace Race as an amateur. Above-average natural cycling ability, though no prodigy-level evidence — he only heard about the Tour de France at 22-23.
inherited_summary: Born to a Crimean Tatar family that was forcibly deported to Uzbekistan during Soviet rule. Active disadvantage of forced displacement and ethnic minority status with no cycling tradition.
ecosystem_summary: Soviet sports school system provided structured cycling training and competition from a young age through the university system. Soviet national team membership gave access to international racing. State-funded full-time athletic development pipeline.

endowment_summary: Talented architect who co-founded a Pritzker Prize-winning firm, but no exceptional early achievement or prodigy evidence. Graduated from ETSAV at 25 and co-founded the practice immediately after. Above-average design ability that emerged through collaborative practice.
inherited_summary: Families were unrelated to architecture. Grew up in Olot, Catalonia, in a modest family. No particular family wealth, domain connections, or architectural lineage documented.
ecosystem_summary: High-trust collaborative trio with Rafael Aranda and Ramon Vilalta at ETSAV (Vallès School of Architecture) became the foundation of RCR Arquitectes. Olot place-based practice in the volcanic Garrotxa region. Catalan architectural culture. The lifelong three-partner collaboration was the key ecosystem advantage.

endowment_summary: Started gymnastics at 5, selected for the elite national training center at 12, and won three Olympic medals at 15. European junior champion with strong performances across multiple apparatus. Exceptional gymnastic talent reaching Olympic medal level as a young teenager.
inherited_summary: Parents Vasile and Virginia Potorac from Bacău, Romania. No particular family advantages or domain connections documented. Four siblings. Modest Romanian family background.
ecosystem_summary: Romanian gymnastics system — the Deva national training center was one of the world's premier gymnastics pipelines. Coaches Marina and Mircea Bibire locally, then Adrian Goreac, Maria Cosma, Octavian Bellu, and Adrian Stan at Deva. Elite institutional access and coaching.

endowment_summary: Started playing tennis at 2, entered first tournament at 4, won 80 official matches by 6. Youngest Grand Slam junior champion at 12 (French Open). Youngest Grand Slam champion in history at 15. Prodigy-level ability with extraordinary hand-eye coordination and tennis IQ.
inherited_summary: Mother Melanie Molitor was a ranked professional tennis player (top 10 in Czechoslovakia) who coached her from age 2 and named her after Martina Navratilova. Father Karol Hingis was ranked 19th in Czechoslovakia. Total tennis family with mother dedicating her life to Martina's development.
ecosystem_summary: Mother's intensive coaching from age 2, move to Switzerland at 7 providing stable training base. Swiss tennis infrastructure. However, the ecosystem was largely mother-driven rather than featuring diverse elite peers or institutions. The mother-coach dynamic was both the ecosystem and the inherited advantage.

endowment_summary: Won European bronze at 18, two European titles (1958, 1959), and Olympic silver (1960). Dominated Czechoslovak skating for a decade (1954-64). Exceptional skating ability, though introduced to the sport by his father rather than showing independent prodigy-level discovery.
inherited_summary: Father Anton Finster was a Hungarian of German descent who introduced him to figure skating and was his first coach through his teenage years. Direct domain immersion through father's coaching. Family changed surname from German-sounding 'Finster' to Slovak 'Divín' after WWII.
ecosystem_summary: Bratislava sports system and Dukla Praha club provided competitive structure. Father's coaching from childhood through 1959, then Ivan Mauer. However, limited elite institutional access compared to Western skaters; post-war displacement and surname change indicate disadvantage.

endowment_summary: Taught chess at 6, won European U10 Girls Championship at 10, World U12 Girls Championship at 12. Won the absolute Lithuanian national championship at 16, defeating multiple grandmasters. Prodigy-level chess ability with world and European youth titles.
inherited_summary: Father Viktor Ivanovič Čmil was a KGB active reserve officer of Russian ethnicity who ran the Šiauliai Chess Club and coached her throughout her early career. Direct domain immersion through father's dual role as club head and personal coach.
ecosystem_summary: Father's chess club in Šiauliai provided early training environment. Lithuanian chess culture and national team access. However, limited access to elite international tournaments or grandmaster-level training partners in early years. Father's coaching was the primary ecosystem advantage.

endowment_summary: Self-taught composer who devoured scores by Bach, Schumann, Ravel, and Debussy. Became organist at Université Saint-Joseph at 14 after his teacher's death. Voracious autodidact with exceptional musical aptitude, though not considered a gifted pianist by traditional standards.
inherited_summary: No family musical tradition; active parental opposition to music. Father wanted him to open a law firm. Family sent him to Jesuit boarding school hoping for medicine, engineering, or law. Active disadvantage of no domain support and parental resistance.
ecosystem_summary: Université Saint-Joseph library and organ access were self-discovered resources. École Normale de Musique in Paris under Henri Dutilleux and Maurice Ohana provided elite training. Paris music scene and orchestration work with major French pop stars. The Dutilleux mentorship was trajectory-changing.

endowment_summary: Raw talent with power and determination. Trained himself in a garage from age 9-10 with makeshift equipment. Three-time Croatian amateur boxing champion. Above-average natural fighting ability but largely self-developed with no formal early coaching.
inherited_summary: Working-class family in Vinkovci, Croatia. Father was an electrician for a railway company who fashioned a crude punching bag from sand and cotton. Father died in 1994 when Mirko was 19. No combat sports lineage. Active disadvantage of poverty and limited resources.
ecosystem_summary: Self-trained in garage with no club behind him. Croatian Army permission to train with national kickboxing team was the key break. K-1 Grand Prix provided the professional platform. However, no elite early coaching, mentors, or institutional access — largely self-created ecosystem.

endowment_summary: Prolific scorer who scored 18 goals in the 1977-78 league season and won the U-21 European Championship. Good natural footballing ability, but started taking football seriously at 16 — relatively late. Above-average talent that developed through the Velež Mostar system.
inherited_summary: Older brother Salem Halilhodžić was a striker at Velež Mostar who insisted Vahid join the club's youth academy at 16. Brother's position at the club provided direct access to the professional pathway. Modest family in Jablanica, Bosnia.
ecosystem_summary: Velež Mostar youth academy — a Yugoslav First League club. Brother Salem's insider position facilitated entry. Yugoslav First League and U-21 European Championship pipeline. The Velež Mostar system was a strong development environment in Yugoslav football.

endowment_summary: Widely regarded as one of the world's best handball players of his generation. Olympic gold at 23, World Championship silver at 21. Exceptional talent recognized by legendary coach Miško Popović who spotted him at a school championship. No one in world handball reached his level.
inherited_summary: Low-income household in Cetinje, Montenegro. Father was a truck driver, mother a teacher — 'they didn't have much time to support me personally.' Active disadvantage of poverty and limited parental support for athletic development.
ecosystem_summary: Metaloplastika Šabac — one of the strongest handball clubs in the world at the time — with the famous 'Šabac Aliens' golden generation. Legendary coach Miško Popović discovered him. Yugoslav national team pipeline. Olympic gold (1984) and European Champions Cup titles. Once-in-a-generation club environment.

endowment_summary: Dominated junior tournaments in Ecuador, turned professional in 1979, won Italian Open at 22, reached world No. 5 by 1984. Exceptional tennis talent with rapid professional rise, though not a globally recognized junior prodigy.
inherited_summary: Father Pedro Pablo Gómez was a prominent radio broadcaster in Guayaquil who directed him to tennis at the Guayaquil Tennis Club to keep him off the streets. Upper-middle class family with access to private club facilities and professional coaching.
ecosystem_summary: Guayaquil Tennis Club with coach Miguel Olvera from age 9. Harry Hopman training. Professional tennis pipeline with rapid rise to ATP Masters titles. Ecuadorian tennis culture at a time when the country produced multiple top players (nephew Nicolás Lapentti reached No. 6).

endowment_summary: Showed unusual musical talent from toddlerhood — could keep time with drumbeats as a toddler, had absolute pitch, received a child's grand piano at 4. Attended Vienna Conservatoire at 16 but left frustrated. Something of a child prodigy, though undisciplined.
inherited_summary: Working-class family in Margareten, a working-class district of Vienna. Father was a machine factory foreman who left the family; mother was a laundry branch manager. Raised by mother after parents separated. Active disadvantage of working-class background and absent father.
ecosystem_summary: Viennese underground club scene provided the platform — played bass in Drahdiwaberl and other bands. Neue Deutsche Welle movement timing was perfect for his breakthrough. However, no elite training (dropped out of conservatoire), no notable mentors, and self-built career through club scene.

endowment_summary: Natural goal-scoring ability — earned £1.50 per goal at amateur level. Developed slowly over seven years at Messina in lower divisions before his breakout Serie B top-scorer season. Above-average talent but not a prodigy; success came through persistence and late development.
inherited_summary: Born in deep poverty in the CEP neighborhood of Palermo, Sicily. Never attended school. Worked odd jobs as a confectioner's assistant and street vendor as a child. Active disadvantage of extreme poverty and lack of education.
ecosystem_summary: AMAT Palermo (amateur bus company team) was his only youth club. Messina in Serie C2 provided seven years of lower-division development. No elite youth academy or early advantages. The Italian football pyramid gave him a pathway, but it was a slow climb from the bottom.

endowment_summary: Multilingual (Italian, Greek, Arabic, French) from cosmopolitan Alexandria upbringing. Self-taught piano and guitar in Paris nightclubs. No prodigy evidence; talent emerged through mentorship and the Saint-Germain-des-Prés artistic circle. Above-average creative ability.
inherited_summary: Parents were Francophile Greek Jews from Corfu who owned the Cité du Livre bookshop in cosmopolitan Alexandria. Educated, multilingual household with strong cultural capital, though not wealthy. Cosmopolitan upbringing provided linguistic and cultural advantages.
ecosystem_summary: Georges Brassens — one of France's greatest singer-songwriters — took him under his wing and introduced him to the Saint-Germain-des-Prés artistic-intellectual circle. Introduction to Édith Piaf led to writing 'Milord,' one of her biggest hits. Paris chanson ecosystem at its peak was once-in-a-generation.

endowment_summary: Compiled a reported amateur record of 241-9. Won Olympic gold at 22 and World Championship bronze at 20. Exceptional boxing talent with an outstanding amateur record, inspired by Muhammad Ali and Yugoslav boxer Mate Parlov.
inherited_summary: Born to a farming family in Jajce, Bosnia. Parents went abroad to work (pečalba) when Slobodan was 4, leaving him and his brothers to be raised by grandparents. Active disadvantage of rural poverty and parental absence.
ecosystem_summary: Older brother Tadija Kačar was an Olympic silver medalist boxer (1976) who started boxing together with Slobodan in 1972. BK Vojvodina in Novi Sad provided club training. Yugoslav amateur boxing system with strong competitive pipeline. Sibling peer relationship was a key ecosystem advantage.

endowment_summary: Won 13 Norwegian national titles and Olympic relay gold, but broke through nationally at 25 — relatively late for an elite skier. Good natural skiing ability built on farm work strength, but not a prodigy. Above-average endurance and fighting spirit.
inherited_summary: Born and raised on a farm in Nes, Akershus — youngest of seven siblings. Farm family in rural Norway with no particular wealth or skiing background. Parents were farmers (father Martin Mørdre, mother Signe). No active disadvantage but no particular advantage either.
ecosystem_summary: Norwegian cross-country skiing culture — the world's strongest tradition. Romerikslagets IL club in Oslo. The 'Jentut'n' relay trio (with Ingrid Aufles and Babben Enger Damon) brought Norway its first Olympic women's cross-country gold. Holmenkollen ski festival tradition.

endowment_summary: First participated in the Hungarian national chess championship at 19, won individual gold at the Chess Olympiad at 23 with an 80% score. Became Hungarian national champion. Exceptional chess ability reaching elite national and international level early.
inherited_summary: Born in Budapest in 1935. No family background details are documented in available sources. No evidence of particular family advantages or chess lineage.
ecosystem_summary: Budapest — a historic center of chess culture with deep Hungarian chess tradition. Strong national team infrastructure and Chess Olympiad competition access. Hungarian chess pipeline provided regular high-level competition and training partners from a young age.

endowment_summary: Started basketball at 14 but showed immediate natural talent — within a year was flashing potential at St. Dunstan's Episcopal. Drafted #1 overall in 1997 after a decorated Wake Forest career. Exceptional late-specialization talent, though not a childhood prodigy.
inherited_summary: Working-class immigrant family from Anguilla on Saint Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands. Mother was a midwife, father a mason. No basketball background. Mother died of cancer when Duncan was 14. Modest circumstances with no domain connections.
ecosystem_summary: Brother-in-law Ricky Lowery (former D-III player) taught him basketball at 14. Wake Forest coach Dave Odom discovered him through a U.S. junior team visit to St. Croix. Wake Forest provided elite college development. David Robinson and Gregg Popovich at the Spurs. However, late start and limited early access.

endowment_summary: Czechoslovak junior national champion at 15. Won World Figure Skating Championships at 17 (1949) and again at 19 (1950). First female to successfully land a double Lutz in competition. Prodigy-level skating ability with two world titles as a teenager.
inherited_summary: Father was a chief advisor (vrchní rada) at the Ministry of Finance in Prague. Mother studied piano and voice at the conservatory. Musical, middle-class family that met at the conservatory. Parents supported skating training, including sending her to London.
ecosystem_summary: Arnold Gerschwiler — renowned Swiss coach at Richmond Ice Rink in London — trained her from 1947. Access to Richmond Ice Rink was a significant advantage over wartime Prague conditions. However, wartime training under blackout conditions was an active disadvantage during developmental years.

endowment_summary: Won Romania's first fencing medal at a major competition with silver at the 1956 World Junior Championships at 20. Olympic bronze at 25. Good fencing ability, but no prodigy-level evidence or exceptional early achievement documented.
inherited_summary: No family background details are documented in available sources. Born in Bucharest, Romania. No evidence of particular family advantages or domain connections.
ecosystem_summary: Progresul Bucharest with coach Angelo Pellegrini provided quality training. Part of a strong generation of Romanian female fencers (Olga Szabo, Ana Pascu, Ecaterina Stahl, Ileana Jenei, Suzana Ardeleanu). Romanian fencing pipeline with World Championship team medals.

endowment_summary: Won over 50 consecutive races between ages 11 and 13, earning the nickname 'El Imbatido' (The Unbeaten). Parents of other children asked him to let others win. Prodigy-level dominance in junior cycling with extraordinary winning streak.
inherited_summary: Father Juan was an amateur bicycle racer who bought him a bike at age 6. Brother Juan Francisco was also an amateur road racing cyclist. Cycling family with direct domain immersion and father as first idol and mentor.
ecosystem_summary: Kelme amateur team and development pipeline with coach Francisco Moya. Spanish cycling culture in Murcia. Puente Tocinos club as youth. The Kelme-Costa Blanca professional squad provided the pathway from amateur to professional. Strong regional cycling infrastructure.

endowment_summary: Won Irish Under-16 Championship as a young teenager. Won both World Under-21 and World Amateur Championships at 20. Only player to win world under-21, world amateur, and world professional titles. Exceptional snooker talent recognized early.
inherited_summary: Working-class Catholic family in Ranelagh, Dublin. Father died of a heart attack when Ken was 13. Limited resources. Active disadvantage of working-class background and early paternal loss.
ecosystem_summary: Jason's Snooker Hall in Ranelagh provided local access. Irish professional Eugene Hughes provided free accommodation and practice time at Ilford Snooker Centre in London. However, largely self-driven with no elite mentors or institutional support — moved to London with £500 to pursue career.

endowment_summary: Started junior races at 14, won 39 times as an amateur from 19 to 23, culminating in Olympic road race gold. Good natural cycling ability with determination and fighting spirit, but no prodigy-level early evidence — breakthrough came through persistence.
inherited_summary: Born on a farm in Denekamp, Overijssel, Netherlands. Grew up with five brothers and one sister. Farm family with no cycling background. Introduction to cycling was riding to school in Enschede. No particular family advantages.
ecosystem_summary: Dutch cycling culture — one of the world's strongest traditions. Ketting-Didam team provided opportunity for international racing. Strong amateur racing pipeline in Twente region and neighboring Germany. Regular competition against quality peers (Neeskens, Nieuwkamp, den Hertog).

endowment_summary: Began observing variable stars at 14, co-authored his first scientific publication at 18 in Acta Astronomica. Received PhD at 24. Prodigy-level scientific ability with early research output and lifelong contributions to astrophysics.
inherited_summary: Father Jan was a lawyer, mother Helena was a Polish literature teacher — both graduates of Vilnius University. Intellectual, educated family with father's private library containing James Jeans' popular astronomy books. Family moved through Kraków, Moscow, and Warsaw, providing broad exposure.
ecosystem_summary: Warsaw University Observatory introduced to him at 14 by professor Włodzimierz Zonn, a family friend. Stefan Piotrowski as doctoral advisor at the University of Warsaw. Access to Lick Observatory in California. However, wartime displacement (Vilnius to Kraków to Moscow to Warsaw) was an active disadvantage during early childhood.

endowment_summary: Admitted to Peking University's elite physics department at age 16, graduated top of his class in 1956. Assigned to China's secret atomic bomb program at 21. Assembled radio receivers from used parts as a teenager. Prodigy-level intellectual ability reaching China's most elite scientific institution as a teenager.
inherited_summary: Father was a railway accountant/postal clerk. Grew up in modest circumstances in Beijing under Japanese occupation. No particular wealth or scientific family background. Active disadvantage of wartime childhood and modest family resources.
ecosystem_summary: Peking University — China's premier university — with professors who were China's top foreign-educated physicists. Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Modern Physics and the secret atomic bomb program. Beijing No. 4 High School. Elite institutional access despite modest family background.
